name: principle-author-is-not-approver
description: Apply to every test, test case, plan, or verdict you produced. A draft is done only after a fresh-context reviewer checks it and after you see each new test fail against a broken version. Your own review, passing tests, and CI are not the independent check.

name: principle-authorize-before-you-look-up
description: Apply when adding or reviewing any endpoint, handler, or resolver that takes an identifier from a caller. Decide whether the caller is allowed before you fetch the thing they named, or the difference between your 403 and your 404 tells them what exists.

name: principle-automate-mechanics
description: Apply across workflows when choosing between agent judgment, existing tools, and saved scripts. Proactively capture stable, repeatable mechanics as verified automation within the requested scope.

name: principle-avoid-tautological-tests
description: Apply when writing or reviewing automated tests, regression tests, expected values, fixtures, mocks, snapshots, property tests, or coverage-driven test additions. Tautological tests are harmful: require an independent test oracle and a credible way for each test to fail under a plausible defect; reject assertions that merely restate production logic, fixture setup, mock configuration, or the value under test.

name: principle-aws-architecture

After selection, use db for database workload diagnosis, schema/access-path tradeoffs, and operations/configuration. Not for public HTT…

name: principle-backend-api-contract
description: Apply when adding or changing a backend endpoint, or an asynchronous event/message. Write or update the OpenAPI (sync) or AsyncAPI (async) contract first and generate server types/stubs from it, instead of writing the handler or publisher/consumer freehand.

name: principle-backend-compat
description: Apply when changing an existing endpoint's request/response shape, an existing event/message schema, or a database migration. Default to additive changes; version or deprecate anything that would break an existing caller, consumer, or deployed row instead of changing it in place.

name: principle-backend-layering
description: Apply before adding business logic to a handler/route, direct DB/ORM/HTTP access outside a repository or external wrapper, or any code that would duplicate a transport/business-logic/data-access split the project already uses elsewhere. Detect whether that split is already established; if it is, match it. If it isn't, say so and skip rather than scaffolding layers a small project hasn't earned yet.

name: principle-backend-performance
description: Apply when adding a hot request path, a goroutine/worker/background job, or anything that can block a request thread or the event loop. Benchmark before/after on a representative load, bound concurrency instead of spawning it unbounded, and don't block the request path on work that doesn't need to finish before the response.

name: principle-backend-security
description: Apply when adding or touching a request/event boundary, an authn/authz decision, a secret, or a third-party dependency in a backend service. Validate at the edge, enforce the specific least-privilege decision, never hardcode a secret, use parameterized queries, and check new dependencies for known vulnerabilities.

name: principle-behavioral-substitutability
description: Preserve supported behavior when implementations, inheritance, extension contracts, or mutable domain invariants change.

name: principle-behavioral-verification
description: Express API and function intent as executable guarantees through the owning boundary; use when writing tests or assessing regression evidence.

name: principle-bind-assigned-ports
description: Apply whenever starting a server, choosing a port, or handing back a URL. Ports are assigned, never chosen. Bind 127.0.0.1 explicitly. Anything the operator opens must be forwarded.

name: principle-bind-to-named-inventory

name: principle-build-the-shared-model-first
description: Use when about to build on someone else's picture (a request, a spec, a resumed plan, another agent's handback), or when agreement on something complex comes too fast.

name: principle-bulkify-by-default
description: Apply to any data operation in Apex or Flow. All operations work on collections; no single-record code paths; trigger and invocable inputs handled as 200-record batches from the first line. Bulkification is necessary but not sufficient for large data volumes.

name: principle-calibrated-uncertainty
description: Apply whenever Jev returns probabilities or confidence, and whenever writing projections, diagnoses, or predictions. Act on high confidence, confirm the middle band, clarify or escalate the low band; never fake certainty.

name: principle-caller-obligations
description: Simplify API use by moving repeatable mechanics to their owner and comparing language builtins; use for caller setup, ordering, lifecycle, or error duties.

name: principle-caption-states-the-conclusion
description: Apply when writing a figure caption for a paper or manuscript. State the finding first, then what the elements are, then n, the test and what the error bars mean.

name: principle-capture-the-baseline
description: WHEN about to change something whose result you will verify or compare; NOT for read-only investigation or syncing a git base; records pre-change evidence so the check reads old value versus new value.

name: principle-central-provider-wiring
description: Apply when every feature Provider or call site must pass the same cross-cutting prop (logger, inspector, telemetry, error boundary, auth): wire it once at a root Provider, with per-site overrides.

name: principle-challenge-from-raw-data
description: Apply when the task treats a belief as given. Reproduce that belief from raw material.

name: principle-challenge-shared-premise
description: Question the premise shared by repeatedly failing fixes and choose an observation that can disprove it before another attempt.

name: principle-challenge-the-brief
description: Apply when a founder states who their customer is, what works, or why deals happen. Check claims against evidence instead of writing them down.

name: principle-change-sync
description: Repeatable workflow for synchronizing APT principle updates across doctrine, checklists, prompts, and references. Use when a principle changes and linked enforcement artifacts must be updated consistently. Triggers: principle update, terminology change, checklist drift, prompt drift, reference contract alignment.

name: principle-chase-y-not-x
description: Apply when a request arrives already shaped as a solution (X): find the real need (Y) behind it before building, and propose a better X when one serves Y.

name: principle-cheapest-layer-that-catches-it
description: Apply when you choose where a test lives. Put each check at the lowest layer where you can observe the failure: static, unit, component or contract, API or integration, end-to-end, then manual or exploratory. Do not repeat one assertion across layers.

name: principle-check
description: Grade a proposed feature, scope change, or design decision against felis's four design principles before any code or doc work begins. Returns a per-principle verdict with the exact failing Test clause for any violation.

name: principle-check-the-facts
description: Use before writing assumptions, a spec, a design or a rollout plan: never build on a business fact nobody confirmed. Lists the business facts a decision rests on and sources each from CLAUDE.md, .fbs/context.md or the user; asks the missing or stale ones.

name: principle-checklist
description: Apply engineering principles as evidence-producing checks at the moment each is cheap — while planning a change (plan), while fixing each review finding (fix), and before commit/PR (finish) — or build a project's own principle list from its PR/MR review history (harvest). Use when starting a non-trivial change, when addressing review feedback, before declaring a change ready, or when a team wants to turn past review comments into checks.

name: principle-ci-cd-and-automation
description: Sets up CI pipelines and their quality gates. Use when creating or modifying a CI pipeline, adding automated checks or test runners to CI, adding preview deploys, or speeding up a slow pipeline.

name: principle-cite-or-delete
description: Apply when writing any claim in a spec, issue, report, or verdict. Every claim carries its source citation, confidence label, and media where applicable. A claim you cannot cite is deleted, not kept with a hedge.

name: principle-claims-rest-on-records
description: Apply before stating any number, status, or citation to the supervisor, when judging a subagent's or tool's report, and when a result looks too good.

name: principle-classify-before-you-fix
description: Apply when a test fails. Name the failure class with evidence before you change anything: product regression, test defect, contract or doc drift, environment, data collision, flaky, or known issue. Do not edit a test or expected value to match the observed behavior unless the class is test defect and the oracle source agrees.

name: principle-clean-architecture
description: Clean Architecture, hexagonal architecture, ports and adapters, and dependency rule. Auto-load when designing architecture, choosing layers, ports, adapters, or keeping the domain free of framework code.

name: principle-clean-architecture-dotnet
description: The layered architecture for a .NET system of this class — Domain / Application / Infrastructure with thin composition-root hosts (API, Worker, UI). Defines dependency direction, what each layer may reference, the patterns this standard deliberately omits, and how SOLID is applied. Use when placing a new type, adding a project reference, or deciding where a concern belongs.

name: principle-clean-code
description: Clean code, DRY, KISS, YAGNI, function length, abstraction level, function argument count, Boy Scout Rule, intent-revealing naming. Auto-load when writing functions, reviewing code clarity, or debating whether to abstract.

name: principle-clean-up-what-you-started
description: WHEN tearing down after a run, verification or failed attempt; NOT for making reruns converge or reverting unrelated edits; releases only resources this run created and keeps the evidence.

name: principle-clear-naming
description: Apply when naming variables, functions, types, files, or endpoints. Enforces the 6-month amnesia test, language conventions, intent-based naming, and cross-boundary consistency.

name: principle-close-or-block-the-dimension
description: Apply at the end of any planning session. Every dimension ends either settled or as a named decision ticket - never merely discussed.

name: principle-code-comment
description: コードのコメントに何を書き、何を書かないかを決めるスキル。コメントには原則として Why not（素直な書き方や代案を採らなかった理由）だけを書き、How はコード、What はテスト、Why はコミットメッセージに任せる。 コードを書く・編集するとき、コメントを書く・直す・消すとき、コメントや JSDoc をレビューするとき、「コメント足して」「コメントいる？」「このコメントどう？」と言われたときは必ずこのスキルを使うこと。テストコードのコメントにも使う。

name: principle-code-first-documentation
description: Treat generated OpenAPI and its documentation UI as part of every HTTP boundary. Mandatory when creating, changing, reviewing, or diagnosing an HTTP server, route, handler, request or response schema, or API error contract.

name: principle-code-quality
description: Load before writing or changing code in any language, and before reviewing a diff, designing types or interfaces, refactoring, or debugging. Covers cross-language limits, naming, code smells, type and boundary discipline, domain modelling, reader load, deletion-first sequencing, and scope rules, plus on-demand references for Python, TypeScript, C#, GDScript, and Godot.

name: principle-code-review
description: Code review heuristics — four-axis review lens (correctness, security, design integrity, test coverage); confidence-based filtering (no finding without a concrete failure scenario); review comment tone (observation over accusation); nitpick filtering; what counts as a real finding vs linter noise. Auto-load when writing or framing a review comment, deciding whether a PR finding is worth surfacing, reviewing a diff for correctness, or filtering review nitpicks.

name: principle-code-review
description: Code review heuristics — five-axis review lens (correctness, security, design integrity, test coverage, comment quality); review comment tone (observation over accusation); nitpick filtering; distinguishing a real finding from linter noise. Auto-load when writing or framing a review comment, reviewing a diff for correctness, or filtering review nitpicks.

name: principle-code-simplification
description: Simplifies working code without changing behavior. Use when code is harder to read or maintain than it should be, or to deslop a branch of AI-generated code patterns. For prose, use unslop.

name: principle-code-speaks-for-itself
description: Apply whenever you write or edit code. Never add a comment that explains the code or your work on it. Say it with names, types, smaller functions, and tests; your work goes in the commit message and the review.

name: principle-codebase-design
description: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.

name: principle-coding
description: 設計・コード・テスト・変更の進め方で判断に迷ったときに参照する、名前で通じる原則の一覧と、原則どうしがぶつかったときの優先順位。コードやテストを書くとき、レビューするときに使う。

name: principle-color-means-one-thing
description: Apply when choosing colours, markers or a colormap for a figure. A condition keeps one colour in every figure, and the figure still reads in greyscale and for colour-blind readers.

name: principle-column
description: Write a short opinion column that names a trend the reader has already noticed, grants it, flips it in one short sentence, defines a principle in two plain sentences, concedes that many reject it, and closes on an assertion plus one hedge. Use this skill for product-management and leadership columns, newsletter opinion pieces, "my take on X" posts, principle explainers, and any 600 to 1,700 word piece for executives and practitioners deciding how to organise; also when the user asks for "a column", "a short opinion piece", "a hot take that still holds up", or "explain the principle behind X".…

name: principle-comments-as-design
description: Use comments as a design tool to capture abstractions, intent, and decisions code can't express. Use when designing a module, interface, or data structure whose intent won't be obvious from the code alone, and when the user asks to "add comments", "document this", or "explain this code".

name: principle-communication
description: Caveman output mode — ultra-terse brief replies with fewer tokens. Strips filler, hedging, pleasantries. Three levels — caveman lite (default), caveman full, ultra caveman / max caveman (maximum compression). Persists until normal mode. Auto-load when the user requests terser output, says "be brief", "less tokens", "caveman mode", "use fewer tokens", or invokes `/caveman`.

name: principle-completion-evidence
description: Before claiming completion, directly verify the final artifact or requested behavior and show the evidence supporting that claim.

name: principle-compose-vue-components
description: Apply when building or refactoring Vue components. Design accessibility first, organize by responsibility, and express layout variants through composition.

name: principle-composition-and-mechanisms
description: Keep feature policy at its composition point and extract mechanisms only for independent obligations; use for assembly and interface boundaries.

name: principle-composition-over-flags
description: Apply when a component, function or API grows boolean props or mode flags: split it into primitives that compose instead.

name: principle-concise
description: Apply to any prose you produce: replies, PR descriptions, commit messages, docs, agent-facing instructions. Short declarative sentences, no filler, no bloat; every sentence earns its place by changing a decision.

name: principle-concurrency
description: Concurrency principles — race conditions, livelock, backpressure, lock-free primitives, choosing between mutex vs channel vs actor vs semaphore vs CAS. Auto-load when designing concurrent code, fixing a deadlock, choosing a synchronization primitive, or reasoning about goroutine/thread/task lifetimes.

name: principle-confidence-from-many-perspectives
description: Apply when you are about to call a design, plan, ticket or root-cause claim done, or a change that would be costly if wrong. Ask how confident you are it will work, and get that confidence from independent reviews, not from your own certainty.

name: principle-conflict
description: Run CLAUDE.md's Principle Conflict Protocol when applying an Engineering Principle would conflict with an existing rule, established pattern, or current implementation — including a violation discovered mid-task. Stops work, explains the conflict, and offers three resolution paths for the developer to choose. Use the moment a conflict is noticed, not after picking a side.

name: principle-constraint-driven-development
description: Constraints — a project's quality bar written down in CONSTRAINTS.md with numbers and commands, and guarded against agents lowering it. Use when setting up quality standards or gates (coverage, security, accessibility, performance), when you need a threshold and have no number, or when an agent silences checks, skips tests, or edits thresholds down to get green.

name: principle-constraint-moves
description: Apply after relief work ships, a checkpoint fires, or metrics shift. Re-identify the binding constraint. Yesterday's bottleneck is not permanently sacred.

name: principle-contain-untrusted-work
description: Treat lower-trust data as data and restrict the authority and resources of code, parsers, plugins, tools, and workers that process it. Mandatory when lower-trust input is interpreted or executed, selects a path, URL, query, or command, or receives access to files, networks, secrets, tenants, or sensitive effects.

name: principle-context-boundaries
description: Prefer local authoritative project evidence and retrieve external information only to resolve concrete factual gaps.

name: principle-contextualize-and-write-for-the-reader
description: Contextualize and write for the reader. Apply when writing anything someone else will read later: a design, a handoff, findings, a report, a verification, a brief, a reply.

name: principle-coordinate-external-effects
description: Move durable intent across transaction and ownership boundaries through explicit delivery, reconciliation, and compensation protocols. Mandatory when committed local work must call a provider, publish a message, control a device, send a notification, or otherwise change an external system.

name: principle-corrections-become-tests
description: Apply whenever a human corrects a label, draft, score or claim.

name: principle-correctness-and-failure-paths
description: Trace correctness and failure paths; preserve error context and recovery ownership when logic, guards, errors, or fallbacks change.

name: principle-correctness-before-speed
description: Apply before you time, report, or keep any kernel change. A perf number counts only after an allclose check and a NaN count pass on the same run.

name: principle-correctness-over-pragmatism
description: Apply when tempted by a shortcut (a cast, a stub, a guard that masks a crash, a downgraded plan): take the structurally correct fix unless the owner explicitly asked for speed.

name: principle-cost-aware-delegation
description: Apply when delegating to subagents, CI or paid APIs: budget turns and scope before the handoff, front-load context, cap scope, and commit passing work before the budget runs out.

name: principle-cost-awareness
description: Cost awareness principles — FinOps mindset, right-sizing, cost-per-request model, storage tier selection, cardinality explosion, log volume. Auto-load when reasoning about cloud costs, right-sizing instances, scale-to-zero trade-offs, or FinOps budget constraints.

name: principle-creation
description: Extract reusable decision-making principles from experiences - especially failures - to build a personal or organizational repository of codified learning.

name: principle-customer-data-stays-home
description: Apply before any list of people or companies goes to an outside tool, such as an enrichment tool, a scraper or a sender.

name: principle-data-modeling
description: Data modeling — relational vs document vs KV vs graph selection, normalization depth, indexing strategy, hot-key avoidance, schema evolution via expand–contract, query-first design, retention and archival. Auto-load when designing schemas, schema evolution, indexing strategy, hot-key avoidance, query-first design, or data retention.

name: principle-data-shape-first
description: Use when logic crosses functions or modules

name: principle-ddd
description: Domain-Driven Design (DDD) — bounded contexts, entities, domain events, and repository pattern. Auto-load when modeling a complex domain, microservice splits, designing aggregates, or aligning code with business language.

name: principle-debugging-and-error-recovery
description: Finds and fixes the root cause of a failure. Use when a test fails, a build breaks, a bug is reported, something that used to work regresses, or an unexpected error or wrong behavior appears.

name: principle-decision-trail
description: Record consequential choices with evidence during long-running, unattended, or multi-session work; preserve pivots without inventing history.

name: principle-decision-trail
description: Apply to long, autonomous, or high-stakes work, and whenever a JEV decision changed the course. Keep a reviewable record of decisions, confidences, and sources.

name: principle-deep-module-design
description: Design modules with simple interfaces and rich implementations. Use when creating, extending, or refactoring any module, class, service or API. Trigger on phrases like "simplify the interface", "reduce API surface", "encapsulate", "clean up boundaries", "split this class", "extract a helper", "wrap this", or before writing the first line of a new abstraction.

name: principle-deep-modules
description: Judge module depth by useful behavior versus caller knowledge and duties; use when evaluating interfaces, hidden mechanics, or seams.

name: principle-deepdive-html-style
description: Generate a single-file deep-dive HTML article in the "principle-deepdive" visual style — dark/light dual-theme, indigo/amber accent palette, inline-SVG hand-drawn diagrams, collapsible cards, citation panels, sticky glass nav, zero external dependencies, offline-readable under 300KB. Use when authoring a long-form analytical HTML article that walks through a topic principle-by-principle with academic citations and visualizations, when the user asks for "principle deep-dive HTML" / "single-file analytical HTML" / "documentation HTML in deepdive style", or when migrating a markdown research not…

name: principle-defensive-history
description: Recover the incident or contract behind unclear defensive code before removing it; missing rationale is not proof it is unnecessary.

name: principle-define-done
description: WHEN starting a multi-step deliverable, phase or plan, or deciding whether one is finished; NOT for single-step answers or choosing which checks to run; sets a checkable completion criterion first and reports every unmet gate.

name: principle-define-errors-away
description: Remove error conditions by redesigning the API instead of handling them. Use when designing an API's error surface, when error handling in a module is getting dense, or when the user asks to "simplify error handling" or "reduce exceptions".

name: principle-define-the-domain-first
description: Use when a new noun, state, or stored field appears, one word is doing two jobs, or two sources use different words for what may be one thing.

name: principle-define-the-question
description: Apply at the start of an analysis, before writing the first query. Write down the decision the analysis serves, the metric definition, the population, the time window, and the result that would change the decision. Without this, analysis drifts into fishing.

name: principle-delegate
description: How to spawn and trust subagents. Use before delegating work, and when a subagent's report comes back.

name: principle-delegate-after-the-contract
description: Assess delegation when work could use separate contexts, parallel execution, or a less capable model.

name: principle-delegate-implementation-review-stays-here
description: Apply when handing work to a subagent. Implementation delegates; design, review, verification, and git mutations stay with the lead.

name: principle-deliver-and-prove
description: Establish readiness to deliver an implementation and verify its expected behavior before editing. Use when beginning implementation or when new findings change what delivery or proof requires.

name: principle-depend-on-caller-contracts
description: Apply when you design a dependency or interface, or call through a collaborator to reach another object.

name: principle-dependencies
description: Dependencies that point one way, onto the language's own tools and stable public APIs, one home for each library, the runtimes a project targets, floating ranges with a pinned lockfile, and deciding logic kept pure.

name: principle-derive-dont-sync
description: Apply when about to store a value that could be computed from existing state, or to keep two copies of one truth in step: derive from one source instead.

name: principle-derive-from-one-owner
description: WHEN the same fact or decision is computed or stored in more than one place; NOT for modelling legal states or collapsing pass-through layers; gives it one owner that other sites derive from or receive.

name: principle-design
description: A design built from proven patterns and SOLID objects that put behaviour with the data it serves, short because it fits the problem.

name: principle-design-for-concurrency
description: Use when actors already overlap: two workers, retries, callbacks, background tasks, or late results can touch the same resource.

name: principle-design-for-failure
description: Use when a call, job, or state change has an effect someone else can see and it can time out, be retried, partly succeed, or end without you knowing.

name: principle-design-for-operations
description: Keeps software correct and identical wherever it runs: crash-only design (fails, stops halfway, runs twice, runs concurrently), idempotent jobs, append-only data runs, and twelve-factor config, logs and releases. Use when writing jobs, pipelines, ETL, workers, CLIs, retries, config, env vars, secrets, logging, deployment or releases.

name: principle-design-foundations
description: Resolve competing design criteria from the current use case, trusted values, ownership, and concrete costs rather than a fixed architecture.

name: principle-design-harness
description: AI エージェントに UI を作らせても品質がぶれないよう、制約・文脈・検証・フィードバックの 4 層で作業環境を整えるための原則。こぎそ氏が提唱した「デザインハーネス」に基づく。

name: principle-design-patterns
description: Design patterns — Gang of Four and beyond. Strategy, factory method, observer, decorator, adapter, facade, template method, command, repository, dependency injection. Auto-load when designing class structure, refactoring toward a pattern, or evaluating whether a pattern applies.

name: principle-design-patterns
description: Design patterns — Gang of Four and beyond. Strategy, factory method, observer, adapter, template method, dependency injection. Auto-load when designing class structure, or evaluating whether a pattern applies.

name: principle-design-system
description: デザインシステムを作る、直す、使うときに、それぞれの要素がどうあるべきかを判断するための原則。基本原則、部品とパターン、トークン、運用の観点。Alla Kholmatova『Design Systems』をはじめ、広く参照される文献に基づく。

name: principle-design-system-first
description: Apply to any UI work. Start from the app's existing design system, tokens, and primitives; a new primitive needs justification. Sweat transitions, alignment, and error states; every feature earns its place.

name: principle-design-the-core
description: Encodes rules in the shape of the data and keeps them in a pure core: sum types, state machines, tables, value objects, parsing at the edge, I/O in thin adapters, ports only where something really varies. Use when choosing types, schemas or data structures, placing new logic, or wiring a database, API, CLI, queue or LLM client.

name: principle-design-to-the-port-not-the-vendor
description: Apply when writing or changing a port's contract, adding a product or a delivery mechanism behind one, naming a config table or glossary term after a product, or writing code that branches on which product or source is in use.

name: principle-deterministic-tests
description: Apply to any test that uses time, randomness, ordering, network, concurrency, or asynchronous UI. The same code and the same inputs must give the same result. Wait on conditions. Do not use fixed sleeps.

name: principle-deterministic-tests
description: Tests that each fail when, and only when, the behaviour they guard breaks.

name: principle-discomfort-is-a-signal
description: Apply when the named constraint feels easy or flattering, or when the owner tours opportunities and activity lists. Prefer the uncomfortable answer. Activity lists are the default dodge.

name: principle-distributed-systems
description: Distributed systems principles — CAP, consistency models (linearizable, causal, eventual, read-your-writes), quorum, leader election, partitioning, idempotency across nodes, fallacies of distributed computing. Auto-load when reasoning about CAP/PACELC trade-offs, choosing a consistency model, ordering events with logical clocks, distinguishing exactly-once delivery from exactly-once effects, designing replication or partitioning strategy, or assessing distributed failure modes.

name: principle-divide-the-work
description: Divide the work when a task splits into independent parts, such as several files, sources, or checks whose results do not depend on each other, or when one step would flood the main thread with bulk output. Give each part to its own subagent and merge short summaries.

name: principle-do-not-block-the-human
description: Apply when tempted to ask 'should I do X?' on reversible work. Proceed, present the result, let the human course-correct after the fact; reserve confirmation for irreversible actions.

name: principle-do-not-block-the-human
description: Aplique quando tiver a tentação de perguntar 'devo fazer X?' em trabalho reversível. Prossiga, apresente o resultado e deixe o humano corrigir o rumo depois; reserve a confirmação para ações irreversíveis.

name: principle-documentation
description: ドキュメントに何を載せ、何を載せないかの原則と事例。リポジトリのドキュメント、エージェント向けの指示ファイル、コードコメントを書くとき、見直すときに使う。

name: principle-documentation-and-adrs
description: Records architecture decisions (ADRs) and the docs around a change. Use when making a decision that's expensive to reverse, changing a public API, shipping user-facing behaviour, or updating a README, changelog, or rules file.

name: principle-dont-invent-problems
description: Applies when a whats-going-on stage decides whether a concern is a problem, whether to classify it, or how sure to be. Do not invent a problem the input does not support.

name: principle-dont-solve-yet
description: Applies when a whats-going-on stage is about to diagnose, brainstorm, or recommend. Stop once the problem is identified.

name: principle-doubt-driven-development
description: Subjects non-trivial decisions to a fresh-context adversarial review before they stand. Use before an architectural decision under uncertainty or a non-trivial commit, when asserting a property you can't prove (safe, idempotent, scales, matches the spec), when working in unfamiliar code, or when the stakes are high or irreversible (auth, security, migrations, deploys).

name: principle-dry
description: 识别并消除知识重复，确保系统中每条知识有唯一权威表示。当需要重构代码、整理文档、优化配置、建立单一数据源时使用。覆盖代码重复、数据冗余、文档重复三大维度，提供具体消除策略和权衡建议。

description: Apply when the outcome should continue with no person feeding the next task. Build the access first.

name: principle-earn-every-element
description: WHEN adding UI controls, settings, options, API parameters or document sections; NOT observing a user journey or weighing scope trade-offs; keeps only elements with a stated user need.

name: principle-enforce-access-explicitly
description: Apply to any data read or write path. CRUD, field-level security, and sharing are deliberate and stated: with sharing on the class, WITH USER_MODE or Security.stripInaccessible() on the data path, and a written reason for every without sharing or system-mode exception.

name: principle-enforce-distributed-authority
description: Prevent stale or competing workers from committing protected changes through atomic claims, conditional writes, and fencing. Mandatory when work can move between workers, leases expire, leadership changes, or failover can leave an earlier actor running.

name: principle-enforce-idempotent-effects
description: Make equivalent requests converge on one logical effect through receiver-side identity and atomic arbitration. Mandatory when a command or external side effect may be delivered or invoked more than once.

name: principle-enforce-where-it-is-stored
description: Apply when more than one client (a web app, an API caller, an agent or MCP tool, an import job) can write the same data, or when a client fills in or corrects a field before sending it. The system that stores the data enforces its rules for every writer; a client that covers for a missing server rule hides the gap.

name: principle-engagement-is-not-consent
description: Apply when a signal such as a like, comment, follow or visit is used as a reason to reach out or to keep data.

name: principle-engineer-tdd
description: Strictly enforce outside-in TDD on every implementation task. Acceptance test first from the issue's EARS/Gherkin scenarios; modules grown via one-behavior RED → GREEN → REFACTOR loops with fake adapters at seams; real adapters earn contract tests; wiring proved by the acceptance test going green. Each step is its own commit per the caller's commit-message template. Encodes scaffold-vs-production boundaries, mandatory edge-case coverage, banned test anti-patterns, and the iron rules.

name: principle-error-design
description: Apply when adding or changing an error: its type, message, public shape, status code or retry guidance. Say what failed and why, end on a way forward, carry typed context, keep reassurance provable, and translate each failure deliberately at the boundary.

name: principle-error-handling
description: Error handling principles — errors as values vs exceptions, wrapping and context chains, retry with exponential backoff and jitter, circuit breakers and bulkheads, log-once boundary discipline. Auto-load when discussing errors as values, retry, exponential backoff, jitter, fail fast, fail soft, idempotent retry, error wrapping, or deadlines.

name: principle-event-driven
description: Event-driven architecture — event sourcing, CQRS, sagas, schema evolution, consumer groups, partitions, idempotent handlers, outbox pattern, dead letter queues. Auto-load when designing event-driven systems, evaluating event sourcing or CQRS, planning saga workflows, implementing idempotent consumers or the outbox pattern, managing dead letter queues, or assessing whether event-driven architecture fits the problem.

name: principle-evidence-in-every-claim
description: Apply to every report, reply, PR body, and review. Each claim carries its evidence or its label (measured, inferred, or guess) in the same sentence. Never report a check you did not run, and never link something you did not open.

name: principle-evidence-not-claims
description: Apply before you report any test status, coverage, fix, or readiness. A verdict must rest on an executed run against the artifact under test, quoted and rerunnable. Proxies such as collect-only, compiling, a dry run, or green CI on another commit are NOT RUN.

name: principle-evidence-over-report
description: When a report and the repository disagree — a worker claims success with no commit, a tracker says done but the gate is red — the repo is right and the report is narrative. Apply whenever consuming status from tickets, workers, comments, dashboards, or pipeline state.

name: principle-redesign-from-first-principles
description: For the Box kitchen project only. Apply when integrating a new requirement into an existing design. Redesign as if the requirement had been a foundational assumption from day one, instead of bolting it on.

name: principle-redesign-from-first-principles
description: 把新需求接进现有设计时使用。

name: principle-redesign-from-first-principles-pi

name: principle-reexecution-safety
description: Prove repeated execution and recovery after partial failure preserve one logical operation without duplicating effects or adopting unrelated state.

name: principle-refactoring
description: Refactoring discipline — Fowler's catalog of behavior-preserving moves (Extract Function, Inline Variable, Move Function, Replace Conditional with Polymorphism, Introduce Parameter Object, Extract Class), the rule of three, characterization-tests-before-touching-legacy, and small-steps-with-green-between discipline. Distinct from principle-clean-code (naming/length aesthetics) and principle-design-patterns (GoF catalog selection). Auto-load when discussing refactoring strategy, code smells, characterization tests for legacy code, or behavior-preserving structural change.

name: principle-refine-mental-models
description: Use when reality surprises the plan, a fix fails twice on the same premise, or the same correction comes twice.

name: principle-refresh-before-resuming
description: WHEN resuming work or acting on a recorded status, handover or earlier claim; NOT for writing a handover before pausing or verifying a new change; re-checks live state and marks stale claims unknown.

name: principle-register-cleanup-before-work
description: Apply when a test acquires a resource that must be released, such as a server, socket, timer, subscription, temporary directory, database, or browser context. Register cleanup immediately after acquisition, before assertions or any other work that can throw.

name: principle-release-engineering
description: Release engineering — semver discipline, rollout strategy, rollback planning, expand-contract for breaking changes, kill-switch, idempotent release automation, post-release verification. Auto-load when cutting a release, planning a breaking API change, writing release notes, choosing a version bump, using a feature flag as a kill-switch, or building release automation scripts.

name: principle-reminder-is-not-a-system
description: Apply when building digests, pings, status bots, or weekly focus messages. Interrogation plus one relief move plus a falsifier beats a motivational ping.

name: principle-replace-internal-apis-atomically
description: Apply when introducing a new internal API while old callers still exist. Migrate callers and delete the old API in the same wave instead of preserving compatibility layers.

name: principle-replace-then-delete
description: Use when replacing an API, table or component

name: principle-report-before-prose
description: Apply when a number, unit, uncertainty, method fact or citation is about to enter the draft. It must be in docs/reports/<topic>/ first, with its source file.

name: principle-report-behavior-not-code
description: Apply when writing any issue, finding, or scenario. Describe the user-visible behavior in the project's domain language. File paths, line numbers, and internal names go stale and make the report unreadable after refactors.

name: principle-report-dont-recommend
description: Apply when presenting options, research findings, or a comparison the person will decide on - a landscape report, an architecture choice, a library pick. Describe tradeoffs and let the person weigh them against context you don't have; don't resolve the decision for them, even with a hedge.

name: principle-report-every-transition
description: WHEN running a long-running loop, watch or babysitting job; NOT for one-off status reports or deciding report structure; reports each meaningful state change unprompted as it happens.

name: principle-report-the-disqualifier
description: Apply when writing or gating any report that makes a causal claim or summarises a cumulative outcome — a backtest, an experiment write-up, a capacity or cost model, a postmortem, an eval summary, a benchmark table. The report must carry what would change the reader's decision: what observation would refute the claim, whether the path crossed a state it could not return from, what the headline was before and after the fix, and which unvaried assumption flips the sign.

name: principle-reproduce-before-report
description: Apply before you claim that a defect exists, file or draft a bug report, or declare a bug fixed. Reproduce it yourself on the closest surface, minimize it, and record the exact conditions. A defect that you cannot reproduce is a lead, not a bug.

name: principle-reproduce-before-you-trust
description: Apply when diagnosing, fixing, or verifying any reported failure. Nothing downstream of a bug report is trusted until the failure is reproduced: same steps, same failure, recorded. An unreproduced report returns to intake, never to diagnosis.

name: principle-reproduce-from-clean-state
description: Apply before reporting a result, handing off a notebook, or merging an analysis. A result counts only when it re-runs from a clean kernel or process, from the source data, with pinned dependencies (uv.lock) and fixed seeds. Hidden notebook state and cell order are bugs.

name: principle-required-changes-only
description: Apply to code changes when strict scope control matters. Change only the lines required to achieve the stated goal. Do not refactor, clean up, reformat, or pre-optimize unrelated code.

name: principle-requirement-fidelity
description: Map behavior and proof to accepted requirements; separate missing, partial, and ambiguous evidence from scope expansion.

name: principle-resilience
description: Code that comes through failure and load by its design: each failure absorbed by its structure or left to fail, each limit known and accepted.

name: principle-resiliency
description: Resiliency principles — fault tolerance, partial failure, failure domains, bulkheads, fail-fast vs fail-soft, health checks, liveness vs readiness probes, idempotency keys, safe retry, deduplication, exactly-once effects, token and leaky buckets, synchronized retries, and 429 responses. Auto-load when isolating dependencies with bulkheads, choosing fail-fast vs fail-soft, configuring health/readiness/liveness probes, making operations safely retryable with idempotency keys or dedup stores, preventing double execution, or adding jitter to prevent thundering-herd retry spikes.

name: principle-respect-the-grain
description: Apply before you join, filter, group, or aggregate a table, and before you trust a total. Name the grain (what one row means) of every table, and check key uniqueness and row counts before and after each step so fan-out and silent drops do not change the number.

name: principle-respect-the-shared-runtime
description: Apply to any Apex transaction design. Governor limits are uncatchable: a breach kills the transaction with System.LimitException and no try/catch recovers it. Design so limits are never approached; probe headroom with the Limits class.

name: principle-respect-transaction-boundaries
description: Limit atomicity and isolation claims to resources in one enforced commit boundary. Mandatory when several changes or effects are claimed to commit or roll back together, a read-then-write invariant depends on isolation, or state and outbound intent are settled together.

name: principle-responses
description: Replies, status updates, questions and reports a person takes in at a glance.

name: principle-responsibility-and-change
description: Place behavior and shared design knowledge with their owner; use when responsibility, dependency direction, or coordinated edits change.

name: principle-reuse-before-building
description: WHEN about to write a helper, owner, script or component; NOT for removing redundancy before an addition or building a tool for uncovered repeated work; finds and uses an existing mechanism, command or action path, or records why new code is needed.

name: principle-reversible-first
description: Apply when choosing how to make a change: prefer the step that can be undone. Park before teardown, power off before delete, warn before enforce, canary before fleet, one rule at a time.

name: principle-review
description: Walk every principle under docs/planning/principles/ and scan the project for contradictions — code, docs, or conventions that violate a principle, principles that contradict each other — and read each principle's own text for being fully descriptive yet succinct. Fans out one subagent per principle via the Workflow tool and writes an HTML report to .sdlc/reports/. With --propose, also lands the text edits it recommends on a branch and opens one PR. Invoke for "review the principles", "do the principles contradict each other", "are the principles too long", or "propose principle fixes".

name: principle-review
description: Review and manage principles in the review queue. Approve, reject, or edit principles distilled from execution trajectories. Triggers on "principle review", "review queue", "approve principle".
allowed_tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash

name: principle-review
description: Load at mandatory review checkpoints (after planning, before opening a PR). Covers both manual and automated principle review protocols.

name: principle-rich-domain-model
description: Apply when writing or changing a business rule for an entity or a domain concept. Behavior lives on the entity, behind intent-named methods and self-validating value objects.

name: principle-risk-before-coverage
description: Apply when you plan, prioritize, select, or cut tests. Spend effort in the order of likelihood times impact and state the risk that you accept. The coverage percentage is a byproduct. It is never the target.

name: principle-room-to-miss
description: Apply when fear of missing is shrinking the attempt. Give the attempt room to fail.

name: principle-root-cause-repair
description: Investigate failures or review causal explanations even without a fix request; validate the failed precondition, trace its first broken guarantee, and identify its responsible owner.

name: principle-route-lessons
description: 失敗や訂正から得た知見をどこに残すか決めるときに適用する。ワークフロー自身の知見は機構（検査・型・スクリプト・手引き）へ、対象のドメインの知見は対象のリポジトリへ。文書に書くだけで済ませない。

description: Protect shared mutable state before parallelizing work.

name: principle-safe-to-rerun
description: Use when code may run twice or stop halfway

name: principle-safety-boundaries-are-hard
description: Apply before weakening any override rule, approval gate, escalation path, or disclosure requirement. Safety boundaries are not tunable by optimization.

name: principle-same-instruments
description: Apply when the draft changes wording and leaves the method alone. Require the tools the best people in the field use.

name: principle-scale-verification
description: WHEN choosing which checks to run on a change; NOT for designing a test's assertions or handling a failing gate; runs every required check and scales extra checks to risk and reversibility.

name: principle-scope-checks-to-the-change
description: Apply before any typecheck, test run, lint, or build. Run only the checks that cover what you changed. Whole-repo gates run only when the operator asks for them.

name: principle-scope-the-session
description: Apply when a session's actual work drifts away from what it was opened to do — a side-investigation becomes the main thread, or an unrelated request gets absorbed into an existing session. Start a fresh session instead of letting scope creep silently expand the one you're in.

name: principle-scoped-attempts
description: Bound repeated attempts at a failing approach and change direction when evidence warrants it.

name: principle-security

Auto-load when designing auth, discussing authn or authz, handling secrets, defining trust boundaries, validating untrusted input, considering SSRF or CSRF, choosing session or JWT mechanics, configuring TLS, picking an encryption primitive, or weighing least-privilege trade-offs.

name: principle-security

description: Hardens code against vulnerabilities (OWASP Top Ten). Use when code handles untrusted input, authentication or sessions, secrets or stored data, third-party integrations or user-supplied URLs, or LLM output; when auditing dependencies or supply-chain risk; or when personal data or privacy compliance (GDPR, CCPA) is involved.

name: principle-seen-success
description: Apply when a goal looks unreachable and one case of it already exists. Point at that case.

name: principle-selective-queries
description: Apply when writing or reviewing SOQL or SOSL. Every query filters on indexed fields with positive operators, returns only the fields needed, and stays selective at production volume: no leading-wildcard LIKE, no negative operators, no formula fields in WHERE without a custom index.

name: principle-self-explaining-code
description: Apply when writing or reviewing any code. No narrating comments; names, types, and structure carry intent. A comment survives only for a non-obvious why the code cannot show.

name: principle-self-explanatory-code

name: principle-separate-author-and-verifier
description: Apply before declaring agent-written code correct. The agent that wrote a change does not grade it. A fresh agent, ideally on a different model, checks it against the original request with its own evidence.

The shape is then extruded upward by the specified height. Examples: - Rectangle: points=[[0,0], [4,0], [4,3], [0,3]] height=2.5 - L-shape: points=[[0,0], [3,0], [3,2], [1,2], [1,3], [0,3]] height=3 - Triangle: points=[[0,0], [2,0], [1,1.7]] height=1

name: probuilder-get-mesh-info

name: probuilder-merge-objects

name: probuilder-merge-objects
description: Combine multiple `ProBuilderMesh` GameObjects into one merged mesh. The first GameObject in the list becomes the merge target. Source GameObjects are deleted by default. Useful for optimizing draw calls and unifying composite props.

name: probuilder-set-face-material
description: Assigns a material to specific faces of a ProBuilder mesh. You can select faces by index OR by direction (semantic selection). This enables multi-material meshes where different faces have different materials. Examples: - Set material on top face: faceDirection="up" - Set material on specific faces: faceIndices=[0, 2, 4]

name: probuilder-set-face-material
description: Assign a material to specific faces of a `ProBuilderMesh`, enabling multi-material meshes (e.g., grass on top, dirt on sides). Supply either `faceIndices` (explicit) or `faceDirection` (semantic); exactly one is required.

name: probuilder-set-pivot
description: Changes the pivot (origin) point of a ProBuilder mesh. The mesh geometry is adjusted so the pivot moves without changing the visual position. Examples: - Center the pivot: pivotLocation=Center - Set pivot to first vertex: pivotLocation=FirstVertex - Set custom pivot: pivotLocation=Custom, customPosition=(0, 0, 0)

name: probuilder-set-pivot
description: Move the pivot (origin) of a `ProBuilderMesh` without shifting the visible geometry. Choose `Center` (mesh bounds), `FirstVertex`, or `Custom` (world-space position). The mesh data is rebaked so the visual position stays fixed.

name: probuilder-subdivide-edges
description: Inserts new vertices on edges, subdividing them into smaller segments. Useful for adding detail to specific edges for further manipulation. Examples: - Subdivide all edges of top face: faceDirection="up", subdivisions=2 - Subdivide specific edges: edges=[[0,1], [2,3]], subdivisions=1

name: probuilder-subdivide-edges
description: Insert new vertices on selected edges of a `ProBuilderMesh`, splitting each edge into smaller segments. Supply either `edges` (explicit list) or `faceDirection` (subdivides all edges of faces facing that direction); exactly one is required.

name: ps-principle-attack-the-premise
description: Apply when two or more fixes that share one premise have failed the same gate. Take a census of which actors hold the imbalance before the next fix, then question the premise instead of writing another fix that assumes it.

name: ps-principle-boundary-discipline
description: Apply when wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Concentrate guards at system boundaries (CLI, config, network, external APIs); trust internal types and keep business logic in pure functions.

name: ps-principle-build-the-lever
description: Apply to any non-trivial work, not just bulk work: edits, migrations, analyses, checks. Build the tool that does it or proves it (codemod, script, generator, or a skill your subagents follow) instead of working by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer can rerun.

name: ps-principle-encode-lessons-in-structure
description: Apply when you catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time, or notice a recurring correction. Encode the rule as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text.

name: ps-principle-exhaust-the-design-space
description: Apply when facing a novel UI interaction or architectural decision with no precedent in the codebase. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare side by side before committing.

name: ps-principle-experience-first
description: Apply when product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs come up. Choose user delight over implementation convenience; ship fewer polished features over more rough ones.

name: ps-principle-explain-the-number
description: Apply before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured: a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result. Find what limits it, and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think.

name: ps-principle-fix-root-causes
description: Apply when debugging. Trace each symptom to its root cause and fix it there; reproduce first, ask why until you reach it, resist nil-check guards that silence crashes.

name: ps-principle-foundational-thinking
description: Apply before writing logic: choosing core types and data structures, sequencing scaffold-vs-feature work, asking what concurrent actors share. Get the data structures right so downstream code becomes obvious.

name: ps-principle-guard-the-context-window
description: Apply when context is filling up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning. Route bulk to subagents; keep summaries in the main thread, not raw payloads.

name: ps-principle-laziness-protocol
description: Apply when refactoring, evaluating diff size, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias toward deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.

name: ps-principle-make-operations-idempotent
description: Apply when designing commands, lifecycle steps, or processing loops that run amid crashes, restarts, and retries. Converge to the same end state regardless of partial prior runs.

name: ps-principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis
description: Apply when introducing a new internal API while old callers still exist. Migrate callers and delete the old API in the same wave instead of preserving compatibility layers.

name: ps-principle-minimize-reader-load
description: Apply when reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Count layers between question and answer, and hidden state in the reader's head; collapse one-caller wrappers and shrink mutable scope.

name: ps-principle-model-the-domain
description: Apply when writing stateful logic, or when code branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files. Encode the domain in a structure instead of scattered conditionals.

name: ps-principle-never-block-on-the-human
description: Apply when tempted to ask 'should I do X?' on reversible work. Proceed, present the result, let the human course-correct after the fact; reserve confirmation for irreversible actions.

name: ps-principle-outcome-oriented-execution
description: Apply during planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture; don't preserve smooth intermediate states with throwaway compatibility code.

name: ps-principle-prove-it-works
description: Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.'

name: ps-principle-redesign-from-first-principles
description: Apply when integrating a new requirement into an existing design. Redesign as if the requirement had been a foundational assumption from day one, instead of bolting it on.

name: ps-principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state
description: Apply when concurrent actors might write to the same file, branch, key, or state object. Eliminate the sharing first; serialize structurally only when one shared writer is a real invariant.

name: ps-principle-sequence-verifiable-units
description: Apply to multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and to how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a verifiable state, check each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself to a reviewer.

name: ps-principle-subtract-before-you-add
description: Apply when sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead weight, redundant validators, and stub references first, then build on the simpler base.

name: ps-principle-test-behavior-not-implementation
description: Apply when you write, change, or keep a test. Call the code the way its users do and assert the result they observe against a literal expected value. If the test would still pass when every imported function returns undefined, rewrite the assertion or delete the test.

name: ps-principle-type-system-discipline
description: Apply when designing types, reviewing a function signature, or writing code in any statically-typed language. The journal requires effect sizes with confidence intervals, full disclosure of exclusions/conditions/measures, and a clear confirmatory/exploratory split, with analysis scripts and data shared. Guides analysis norms; it does not fabricate results.

name: psci-literature-positioning
description: Use when positioning a Psychological Science manuscript against the literature within the journal's tight word budget. With roughly 40 references and a 2,000-word Introduction+Discussion, positioning must be sharp — establish the gap and the contribution fast. Stakes the contribution; it does not write the literature review.

name: psci-open-science-and-transparency
description: Use when meeting Psychological Science's open-science requirements. For submissions on or after 1 January 2024 the journal requires open data and materials (case-by-case exemptions), a Research Transparency Statement placed between the Introduction and Methods, persistent identifiers for shared content, and treats transparency limits and preregistration quality as factors in editorial decisions. Prepares compliance; it does not waive requirements.

name: psci-rebuttal
description: Use when writing the response to a Psychological Science revise-and-resubmit. Reviews here often demand added robustness, fuller disclosure, or stronger transparency, so the response must address every point and strengthen credibility without breaking the tight format. Structures the response letter; it does not fabricate new results.

name: psci-review-process
description: Use when you need to understand how Psychological Science evaluates a manuscript — anonymized peer review, editorial weighting of robustness, transparency, and preregistration quality, desk-reject and decline-without-review patterns, and the Registered Reports route. Use when stress-testing a paper before submission or interpreting a decision letter. Sets expectations and shapes the paper to survive review; it does not contact editors.

name: psci-review-process
description: Use to understand how Psychological Science evaluates a manuscript — anonymized peer review, editorial weighting of robustness, transparency, and preregistration quality, and the Registered Reports route. name: psci-study-design
description: Use when designing studies for a Psychological Science manuscript so they meet the journal's standards for power, sample-size justification, preregistration, and confound control. Strengthens the design and pre-analysis plan; it does not write code.

name: psci-submission
description: Use when running the final pre-submission preflight for Psychological Science via Manuscript Central — word-format compliance, the 150-word structured abstract, APA 7th-edition style, anonymization, the Research Transparency Statement, and open data/materials with DOIs. Final checks; it does not draft content.

name: psci-tables-figures
description: Use when building tables and figures for a Psychological Science manuscript. The journal uses APA 7th-edition style and asks that tables and figures be embedded within the main text near where they are discussed, and exhibits should show effect sizes and uncertainty. Designs exhibits; it does not run the analysis.

name: psci-theory-and-hypotheses
description: Use when stating the theory and hypotheses for a Psychological Science manuscript. The journal's credibility norms require a clear separation of confirmatory (preregistered) from exploratory analyses and theory stated before results. Structures the argument; it does not run analyses.

name: psci-topic-selection
description: Use when deciding whether an empirical psychology project fits Psychological Science and which manuscript type to target. The journal favors concise, high-impact, well-powered work whose claims are robust and broadly relevant. Frames the question; it does not collect data.

name: psci-workflow
description: Use when starting or navigating any Psychological Science manuscript and you are unsure which sub-skill applies. Use when choosing among manuscript types or returning with a decision letter. Routes by lifecycle stage and manuscript type (Research Article, Registered Report Stage 1/2, Registered Report with Existing Data, Commentary), and flags the journal's tight word format and open-science requirements. It dispatches; it does not draft content.

name: psci-workflow

name: psci-writing-style

name: ptolemy-annual-atmosphere
description: 年、季、月与天象的气候推演。当用户问“今年／这季的天气收成怎么推”“按托勒密怎么读云霞晕虹”或要按星座气候本性推演一个时段的大气状况时使用。以年新月为起点，先取季度前最近的新月／满月排盘读主星，再逐月、逐日推演，最后用日月升起落下、晕、虹等征兆微调。只作倾向性描述，不作具体天气预报。

name: ptolemy-aspects
description: 星座间关系（相位）读法。当用户报了出生信息，要问两个星座/两颗行星之间是什么关系——对冲、三分、四分、六分，哪种和谐哪种冲突；或问"命宫/服从宫""互视等力""隔绝"这类星宫关系时使用。需要出生信息；没有出生信息不激活。

name: ptolemy-birth-circumstances
description: 托勒密论出生当时的情形。当用户提供出生（或受孕）信息、要按古典占星看"这一胎是男是女""会不会是双胞胎""出生有无畸形或缺陷""孩子能不能养大"时使用。按《Tetrabiblos》第三卷第七至第十章：性别看两个发光体与上升的阳性/阴性倾向；孪生看双体星座；畸形看发光体与上升失联、凶星占角；"能否养育"看凶星对发光体的围困。需要出生信息。含未成年死亡一类的敏感段落，只转述古代文本的判法，绝不作任何寿命或死亡断言；涉及孕期与新生儿健康一律不替代就医。

name: ptolemy-body-and-disease
description: 托勒密论形体体质与身体的伤病。当用户提供出生信息、要按古典占星看"我的形貌与体质""古典里身体的伤、损、病怎么看"时使用。按《Tetrabiblos》第三卷第十六章（形体与气质）与第十七章（身体的伤、损、病）：看上升与月亮及其主星定形体，看地平东西两角被凶星配置定伤病，并给出各行星主管的身体部位。需要出生信息。涉及健康一律不作医疗判断、不替代就医。

name: ptolemy-dignities
description: 行星在星座中的"权柄"读法。当用户报了出生信息，要问某颗行星落在某星座"是有力还是无力"——是否入庙、入旺、是否在其三分性里、是否落在自己的界（terms）、以及界的起点怎么算时使用。需要出生信息；没有出生信息不激活。

name: ptolemy-fate-calibration
description: 命定说法校准工具：当用户拿着一句占星/算命的断言（"35 岁有大劫""星盘说我注定离婚""这颗凶星会害我"）或追问"占星准不准、是不是注定"时，用托勒密《四书》卷一第 1-3 章他自己定下的限度——规则不可能确定无误、只看天象而不顾其他原因的预判必然不完整、弱的倾向可被对冲、预知的用处是事先准备——把断言拆开、降级成条件句，再补上现代证据和一件现实中值得做的准备。 触发信号："算命的说我今年有劫，是真的吗""星盘是不是注定的""占星到底准不准""托勒密自己信宿命吗""有人说要花钱化解""这个预言让我很害怕"。 不触发场景：想要具体读盘（行星强弱、职业、性格）→ ptolemy-planet-condition / ptolemy-topic-ruler / ptolemy-mind-temperament；问今年行运 → astrology-transit；八字流年断语 → bazi-liunian（可借用本 skill 的校准步骤）；周易"吉凶"词义 → auspicious-risk-language；恐惧已影响睡眠或反复追问 → psyche；自伤念头 → `cross-system-hub` C5 危机话术；问寿命 → fortune 第五节第 6 条；不害怕，只想把一句倾向变成能验证的概率、设复盘日 → forecast-calibrate-claim。

description: 恒星（黄道内外）的性质取用。当用户报了出生信息，问某颗恒星/星团（如角宿一、心宿二、毕宿五、轩辕十四、昴星团、大角星）对某主题的作用，或想按《四书》给恒星"像哪颗行星"的脾性时使用。需要出生信息；没有出生信息不激活。

name: ptolemy-friends-and-enemies
description: 朋友与敌人的星盘推演。当用户给出出生信息、问"我和某人合不合""为什么总跟某个人合不来""谁会是我的贵人 / 小人"时使用。合看双方盘里日 / 月 / 上升 / 福点四处，判长久的朋友或敌人，并看哪些星造就哪一种交情；只在象征层做倾向性推演，不替用户给真实的人贴标签、不替用户做断交 / 交友的决定。

name: ptolemy-general-event-eclipse

name: ptolemy-mind-quality-and-disorder

name: ptolemy-mind-temperament

name: ptolemy-planet-condition
description: 托勒密古典"行星状态"评估工具：用《四书》卷一的四性、吉凶、昼夜派别、五种尊贵（庙/三分性/旺/界/相位）和强弱规则，判断本命盘里某颗行星是"在主场"还是"在客场"、表达得顺还是要绕路。用户已有星盘数据、想用古典规则看某颗行星或整体结构时激活；也是 ptolemy-topic-ruler 与 ptolemy-mind-temperament 的底层步骤。 触发信号："用古典占星看看我的土星""我的金星是入庙还是落陷""托勒密怎么看我的盘""哪颗行星在我盘里最有力""我的火星是不是很凶""吉星凶星是什么意思"。 不触发场景：只想看太阳/月亮/上升三要素或土星回归、今年行运 → astrology-transit；问职业/财富/友谊某一主题 → ptolemy-topic-ruler；问性格心性 → ptolemy-mind-temperament；问"是不是注定" → ptolemy-fate-calibration；问寿命、疾病、事故、择日 → 拒绝该部分（fortune 第五节），其余照常；没有出生数据 → fortune 路由（周易/塔罗）。 降级：只有出生日期、没有时间 → 只读星座层尊贵，不读宫位与昼夜派别，并注明精度不足。

name: ptolemy-planet-natures

name: pytcr-bulk-repertoire-metrics

Use after pytcr-bulk-data-loading, once the standardized repertoire table (df) is available.

name: pytcr-bulk-repertoire-overlap
description: Compare clonotype repertoires pairwise across many bulk TCR-Seq samples with pyTCR — Jaccard index, overlap coefficient, Morisita-Horn index, Tversky index, cosine similarity, Pearson correlation, relative overlap diversity, geometric-mean overlap frequencies, and Jensen-Shannon divergence of V-gene usage, each as a sample-by-sample heatmap. Use after pytcr-bulk-data-loading, once the standardized repertoire table (df) has 2+ samples.

name: pytcr-data-loading

Use after pytcr-clonotype-clustering, once clonotype/cluster IDs and cell-type annotations exist in mdata.obs.

name: pytcr-gex-integration

name: python-clean-architecture-interface-segregation
description: Instructs the agent to satisfy the Interface Segregation Principle (clients shouldn't depend on operations they don't use) as an automatic consequence of functional dependency inversion — pass or bundle only the specific Callable functions a piece of code actually needs, never a class implementing unused methods or raising NotImplementedError for operations that don't apply. Extends python-clean-architecture-dependency-inversion with the ISP-specific framing.

name: python-clean-architecture-open-closed
description: Instructs the agent to achieve the Open-Closed Principle (extend without modifying existing code) using functools.singledispatch over immutable dataclasses instead of abstract base classes and subclass polymorphism — new "shapes"/variants register a new implementation without touching the original dispatcher function. Includes the honest expression-problem tradeoff against structural pattern matching, which is simpler for a genuinely closed set of variants but requires touching the central function to add a new one.

name: python-clean-architecture-presenters
description: Instructs the agent to implement presenters as plain functions (a Callable type as the "port," concrete formatting functions as the implementations) instead of an ABC with private formatting methods on concrete subclasses — and to apply the Humble Object pattern by keeping views (CLI print functions, templates) free of all formatting logic, pushing every formatting decision into presenter functions where it stays independently testable.

name: python-clean-architecture-request-response-models
description: Instructs the agent to implement request/response DTOs as frozen dataclasses with __post_init__ validation, and their transformations (external format to domain params, domain entity to external format) as free functions rather than instance/class methods — keeping the same boundary-translation purpose (validate and convert inbound data, shape and protect outbound data) with this repo's consistent function-based calling convention.

name: python-clean-architecture-scaling
description: Instructs the agent to treat Clean Architecture as a spectrum of independently-adoptable patterns, not an all-or-nothing structure — right-sizing adoption to a Python project's actual size and complexity, starting small projects with a simple but modular layout (separate business logic from presentation, inject dependencies, define clear interfaces) and evolving toward the full layered structure only as growth actually justifies it. Prevents both under-engineering (tangled small scripts) and over-engineering (full four-ring ceremony for a throwaway script).

name: python-clean-architecture-screaming-architecture
description: Instructs the agent to organize a Clean Architecture Python project's top-level structure around business domain and use cases, not frameworks or technical layers — a directory listing should scream "online bookstore," never "FastAPI app." Covers the concrete naming/layout test, and the underlying benefits (protecting the investment in domain logic, mock-free testability, technology swappability, and fit with Agile/CI/CD) that justify the pattern to a team.

name: python-clean-architecture-single-responsibility
description: Instructs the agent to apply the Single Responsibility Principle at the function/module level, not the class level — a dataclass holding only its core fields, with each group of operations that has its own "reason to change" living in its own module of plain functions. Includes the balance warning against over-fragmenting into too many tiny modules, and why SRP-sized functions are trivial to test.

name: python-clean-architecture-substitutability
description: Instructs the agent to apply the Liskov Substitution Principle as substitutability of functions sharing a Callable type, not substitutability of subclasses — any function matching a given Callable signature must honor the same behavioral contract (same meaning of inputs/outputs, same error semantics) as every other function matching that signature. Reformulates the classic Vehicle/inheritance violation as composition via a passed-in "operation" function, not a base-class contract.

name: python-clean-architecture-test-doubles
description: Instructs the agent to test use cases, controllers, and presenters by passing plain stand-in functions instead of unittest.mock.Mock(spec=SomeABC) — there is no ABC left to spec against once dependencies are Callable types, and a stand-in is just a function literal or a small recording closure. Covers verifying calls without Mock's assert_called_once_with, pytest fixtures that build plain dataclasses/functions instead of Mock objects, parameterized testing of pure functions, and freezegun for time control — all composing naturally once dependencies are already plain functions.

name: python-clean-architecture-testing-strategy
description: Instructs the agent to concentrate test coverage where Clean Architecture's boundaries make it cheap — pure domain/use-case functions get exhaustive unit tests with zero setup, integration tests exercise one real boundary at a time (a real driver, with peripheral concerns stubbed) rather than the whole system, and end-to-end tests stay few. Test file structure mirrors the architecture's layer packages, making an awkward test import itself an early warning of a Dependency Rule violation.

name: python-clean-architecture-use-cases

Covers multi-step orchestration, ports for external services, adapters for third-party services (also just functions), and optional/pluggable dependencies passed as parameters instead of a mutable registered-services dict.
